title: CanSahyogi - In-Hospital Handholding & Counseling
text: CanSahyogi - In-Hospital Handholding & Counseling (Patient Care): Handholding and emotional counseling sessions in regional hospital premises for cancer patients, led by certified cancer victors. title: Nutrition During Chemotherapy (CanAhaar Clinical Protocol)
text: Nutrition During Chemotherapy (CanAhaar Clinical Protocol) (Clinical Nutrition): During chemotherapy, high protein intake (1.2 to 1.5g per kg) is essential to preserve muscle mass and recover white blood cell counts. Eat small frequent meals (5-6 meals/day). Prioritize steamed lentils, boiled eggs, paneer, and lightly cooked vegetables. Avoid raw unwashed salads, unpasteurized milk, or street food due to neutropenic infection risks. Stay hydrated with tender coconut water, diluted buttermilk, and warm ginger tea to combat nausea. Source: CanAhaar Clinical Nutritional Protocol, Sanjeevani

title: Managing Chemotherapy Nausea and Taste Alterations
text: Managing Chemotherapy Nausea and Taste Alterations (Symptom Management): To manage chemo nausea: eat food at room temperature (warm foods emit strong odors that trigger nausea). Use non-metallic plastic or wooden utensils if experiencing metallic taste (dysgeusia). Rinse mouth with warm water containing a pinch of baking soda and salt before meals. Take prescribed anti-emetics 30 minutes before meals. Source: Research Report by Monk Prayogshala - Importance of Holistic Wellness

title: Managing Anxiety Before Scans and Chemo (Pre-Scan Panic)
text: Managing Anxiety Before Scans and Chemo (Pre-Scan Panic) (Psychosocial Support): Pre-scan anxiety ('scanxiety') is a normal psychological response. Evidence-based coping methods include: 4-7-8 rhythmic breathing (inhale 4 seconds, hold 7 seconds, exhale slowly 8 seconds) to activate parasympathetic nervous system and drop heart rate; grounding exercise (name 5 things you see, 4 you can touch, 3 you hear, 2 you smell, 1 you taste); speaking with a Sanjeevani Cancer Buddy victor who has undergone the same procedure. Source: Research Report by Nirmala Niketan - Importance of Psychosocial Support

title: Government Financial Schemes for Cancer Care (Ayushman Bharat, PMNRF, RAN)
text: Government Financial Schemes for Cancer Care (Ayushman Bharat, PMNRF, RAN) (Financial Schemes): Financial assistance available in India includes: 1) Ayushman Bharat (PM-JAY) providing up to Rs 5 Lakhs per family per year for secondary and tertiary hospitalization. 2) Rashtriya Arogya Nidhi (RAN) providing financial assistance up to Rs 15 Lakhs for BPL patients treated at designated government super-specialty hospitals. 3) Prime Minister National Relief Fund (PMNRF) providing partial grant assistance on application through treating hospital medical superintendent. Sanjeevani counselors assist in document filing free of cost. Source: CanDaan Scheme Navigator & Sanjeevani Annual Yearbook 2025

title: Recognizing Warning Signs and Early Detection (CanChetna)
text: Recognizing Warning Signs and Early Detection (CanChetna) (Cancer Awareness): Early warning signs of common cancers: 1) Breast: painless lump, dimpling of breast skin, nipple inversion or discharge. Practice monthly Breast Self-Examination (BSE) 5-7 days after period ends. 2) Oral: non-healing mouth ulcer lasting over 2 weeks, white/red patches (leukoplakia), difficulty swallowing or opening mouth. 3) Cervical: unusual bleeding between periods or after intercourse, persistent foul discharge. 4) Colorectal/Lung: persistent cough lasting over 3 weeks with blood, sudden unexplained weight loss, change in bowel habits. Source: CanChetna Public Awareness Handbook, Sanjeevani
